title: Scarcity
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:47Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Both bank cards cover scarcity but go beyond this Year 7 brief: one adds factors of production and opportunity cost, and the other adds the what, how and who questions at senior secondary depth, so neither fits as it is or with small changes.

draft.title: Scarcity
card: Resources are the things used to make goods and services. Land, labour (people's work), money and time are all resources.
Resources are limited. There is only so much land, so many workers, so much money and so many hours in a day.
People's wants have no end. When one want is met, a new one often appears.
Scarcity is the problem that limited resources cannot meet unlimited wants. Because of scarcity, not every want can be met.
draft.remember: Scarcity: limited resources, unlimited wants, so not every want can be met.

opts: Resources are limited but wants are unlimited
Resources are unlimited but wants are limited
People have no needs and only have wants
Shops sometimes run out of the goods people want
a.why: Scarcity is the gap between limited resources and unlimited wants. A shop running out of stock is a short-term problem for one seller, not the idea of scarcity itself.
a.clue: Think about which side has an end and which does not.

b.q: Priya has $50 in savings and one free Saturday. She wants new headphones, a day at the beach and a game. Why can she not have all three?
opts: Her money and time are limited but her wants are not
Her wants are limited but her money is unlimited
Headphones, beaches and games are not real wants
She has not worked hard enough to afford them
b.why: Priya has only so much money and time, and her wants are greater than both. That is scarcity. Working harder might give her more money, but resources would still be limited.
b.clue: Look at what Priya has a limited amount of.

a.best: Resources are limited but wants are unlimited

b.best: Her money and time are limited but her wants are not
